records.reason: m160 at 2/1, 100 ul, 400 ul DCM gives a matched-condition point for the m161 choice. Measured m160 at 2/1 and 50 ul was 14.14/34.07 mL (b21061720e23b7a5bdcb), while m161 at the same ratio and 150 ul was 10.94/31.43 mL (0ced19fd8372ed93361c). This tests isomer-specific response and loading transfer.

Matched to 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f for the positional m160/m161 comparison. The label can determine whether the current similarity representation transfers onset and completion between the two aminobenzonitrile isomers.

m160 at 0/1 and 150 ul supplies a weak-eluent baseline for the isomer pair and brackets the stronger-retention m160 observation b4e0e9dc92fca2c88b90. It tests whether the onset and completion transition begins at the predicted location.

m199 at 5/1 and 50 ul probes the middle of a potentially sharp sulfoxide response. The measured 10/1 point aa83ae83c0fa0cc37777 was much later and broader than predicted, whereas the measured 2/1 point d49f2ae16cf70d54ccf4 was early. This local point discriminates a steep ratio transition from a loading artifact.

The weak-eluent m199 point at the same nominal loading complements f82cfd3b57735b0ead3c. Together they anchor the low-to-intermediate branch around the contrasting measured m199 records aa83ae83c0fa0cc37777 and d49f2ae16cf70d54ccf4.

m37 at 20/1, 50 ul tests a high predicted late-retention branch at lower loading. The measured 20/1, 150 ul record 3b2c663a28a9f32bd1d3 was 43.30/94.86 mL, so this label isolates loading transfer within a strongly polar nitro-ketone scaffold.

m37 at 10/1 and 100 ul fills the intermediate ratio region before the measured late 20/1 point 3b2c663a28a9f32bd1d3. It can teach whether both endpoints rise together or whether completion broadens selectively.

m90 at 5/1 and 100 ul probes the onset of the pyridine-containing ester branch. The measured m90 point 96710afeabc594baa359 at 10/1 and 100 ul was 48.17/107.99 mL, while the 2/1, 50 ul record 6a4e95d2a3cca31094a1 was much earlier. This tests transition curvature.

m90 at 10/1 and 150 ul extends the high-retention branch and tests whether the measured 10/1, 100 ul delay 96710afeabc594baa359 transfers with loading. The endpoint-specific label is especially useful because the current prediction has a broad V2 span.

m211 at 50/1 and 50 ul explores a high-eluent heteroaromatic branch. Measured m211 points at 5/1 and 20/1 (1ce749f818905d3c61d4 and 434e465cfa7e0034f233) provide lower-ratio anchors but do not establish the high-ratio slope.

m211 at 20/1 and 100 ul supplies an intermediate point between the measured m211 records 1ce749f818905d3c61d4 and 434e465cfa7e0034f233. It tests whether the model's large predicted transition is scaffold-specific or transferable from related nitrogen-containing aromatics.

m146 at 10/1 and 100 ul targets the quinoline branch where the measured 10/1, 150 ul point 23ef03f3e75e40b20095 was 51.34/108.46 mL. Comparison with the measured 2/1 point 2745c6978a8911fc3dda tests the ratio response and completion growth.

m146 at 5/1 and 150 ul fills the lower-ratio side of the quinoline response before 9e3ce3497298084abd83. It provides a high-value local curve point for a family with repeated large onset and completion errors.

m118 at 2/1 and 100 ul tests the irregular early-to-intermediate branch. Measured m118 spans 4.78/36.82 mL at 10/1 (319e89d7000731f64e7f), 19.16/30.41 mL at a higher loading (ea004678fc850c759752), and 56.20/117.46 mL at 50/1 (2d178efe0181baca2bd5).

m135 at 5/1 and 50 ul explores an underconstrained aromatic alcohol branch. Strongly delayed measured alcohol analogues m206 and m207 (b7cf293311f83700cd9a and a19f98569910dc7fd6c4) suggest that donor-containing scaffolds need local labels rather than generic ketone transfer.

m135 at 10/1 and 150 ul extends the same alcohol family across ratio and loading. The paired label can separate a ratio-driven delayed branch from a loading-associated broadening effect seen in related alcohols.

m206 at 5/1 and 100 ul fills the response region below the measured 10/1, 150 ul point b7cf293311f83700cd9a. It tests whether the naphthyl alcohol's large V1/V2 values emerge gradually or through a scaffold-specific transition.

m207 at 10/1 and 150 ul extends the bromobenzyl alcohol response beyond measured points a19f98569910dc7fd6c4 and a7906197994af5c86745. This constrains transfer across loading and distinguishes onset movement from completion broadening.

m209 at 50/1 and 150 ul is a high-eluent phenol test following the measured 50/1, 100 ul point 13ba7659fc6b864608f8. It probes whether completion remains late with increased loading and whether donor-containing phenols share a common high-ratio response.

m212 at 5/1 and 150 ul supplies a loading contrast to the measured 5/1, 100 ul point 252c027cf5a42b92c953 and a ratio contrast to 942b8fc9cf013acda52b. This tests conditional retention of an amine-containing diaryl scaffold.

m216 at 10/1 and 50 ul targets the quinoline-like high-retention family. The measured 10/1, 100 ul point 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321 and 2/1, 100 ul point e7bf6bd74f8498f1cb11 provide anchors for both loading and ratio response.

This m216 point holds the ratio fixed against e47aebe2660b9e1528de but raises loading to 150 ul. The paired labels test whether the broad predicted interval is loading-sensitive, using measured m216 evidence at 10/1 and 2/1 as context.

m87 at 50/1 and 100 ul extends a donor-containing ester branch beyond the measured 20/1 and 50/1 low-loading points eed75e5b0d9c27fa754c and 810b16f35a3a86f451ce. It can repair high-ratio endpoint slopes.

m88 at 1/1 and 100 ul provides a lower-ratio, moderate-loading point for a strongly polar amino ester. It complements the measured 2/1 low-loading point 27d20ccfd8f7234015f4 and the delayed 5/1 point 85924bdd0693438dc23a.

m89 at 50/1 and 100 ul tests a high-ratio branch for the amino ester family. It can be compared with the measured lower-ratio PE point e513420e1b7414424e7c and high-loading observations to learn whether V2 broadening transfers.

m198 at 20/1 and 50 ul probes the middle of a nitrobenzaldehyde response. The measured 0/1 point 3232c07325c3dd8f1e6a was early, while the measured 50/1 point 8ab554cd154e9749790b was 41.16/92.81 mL; this label tests the transition shape.

m114 at 50/1 and 150 ul is a loading extension of the measured high-ratio point 44fcf641ccfa3b10a97c, whose completion was 75.88 mL. It teaches whether the late benzophenone branch is stable across loading.
m114 at 20/1 and 50 ul supplies a lower-ratio endpoint-specific point against the measured 20/1, 100 ul record 8232ed63909910ce88f2. The pair can constrain onset and completion separately.

m45 at 5/1 and 150 ul fills the acid response between the measured 20/1 point 53a9a2469f8d4ead8732 and the discordant 50/1 record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848. It tests whether the unusual weak-eluent label is an isolated failure or part of a structured curve.

m11 at 20/1 and 150 ul probes the high-polarity nitrogen branch between measured 20/1 and 50/1 records 2f48e798c7917fb7d2ae and 9ffee2813aef5c26f96f. The label is useful for learning a completion response that is not captured by ordinary polarity descriptors.

m72 at 20/1 and 150 ul with 200 ul DCM extends the loading-protocol experiment. Prior matched-ratio measurements with DCM and PE, 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327, 8e7636d7a60a6058305a, and 754f1d33b0ed61557754, show that onset and completion may respond differently.

m197 at 10/1 and 50 ul explores a donor-containing aromatic aldehyde branch. Measured m197 at 10/1 and 150 ul (70abe1d9543e6cae908e) and at 50/1 and 50 ul (619663c2b3ffb3a6c497) provide endpoint and ratio context for this lower-loading point.

hypotheses.content: Strongly retained polar, acceptor-rich, heteroaromatic, or multifunctional scaffolds have scaffold-specific condition responses. A global late-retention correction is insufficient because some branches shift both endpoints while others mainly broaden completion.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected heteroaromatic, nitro, amino, sulfoxide, and pyridine-containing rows expose shared descriptor limits and can improve structure-condition interactions across many catalog families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do these high-retention branches follow smooth ratio curves within scaffold, or do connectivity and donor/acceptor arrangement create separate response regimes?

hypotheses.content: Connectivity and positional isomerism can change solvent-response slopes and endpoint widths even when descriptors and broad functional groups are similar.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched m160/m161 and m211 experiments can teach the graph representation which local connectivity differences matter for V1 and V2 response rather than only for absolute retention.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched loading and ratio, do the isomers differ mainly in onset, completion, or interval width?

hypotheses.content: V1 and V2 have distinct condition responses; increased solvent strength or loading can leave onset nearly unchanged while moving completion substantially.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m114 and other endpoint-focused contrasts provide training signals that prevent the model from using one shared correction for onset and completion or treating interval width as uncertainty.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: For high-width benzophenone and aldehyde branches, which endpoint is most sensitive to ratio and which is most sensitive to loading?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading protocol have conditional effects that may differ by scaffold and endpoint; some matched contrasts show protocol sensitivity while others show little response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m72 and m216 loading contrasts can distinguish transferable loading effects from isolated protocol or label variation and reduce inappropriate extrapolation across repeated catalog conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched protocol or loading changes produce repeatable endpoint shifts within a molecule, or are they dominated by scaffold-specific and unrecorded effects?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic alcohols, phenols, and donor-containing aldehydes can form delayed or unusually broad silica-retention branches that do not transfer reliably from non-donor analogues.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The alcohol, phenol, and amino-ester choices add labels in a chemical region where hydrogen bonding and positional environment may be underrepresented by current features, improving donor-sensitive generalization.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are delayed branches shared across alcohol and phenol families, or do aromatic position and neighboring acceptors determine the response independently?

hypotheses.content: Acidic and strongly hydrogen-bonding carbonyl compounds require local ratio curves because isolated records can show sharp transitions or anomalous completion labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m45 and m11 points constrain rare but high-impact response regions and help the retrained model avoid spreading one anomalous acid or polar-carbonyl label across unrelated rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the acid and polar-carbonyl branches show smooth endpoint-specific curvature, or are some apparent transitions irreducible record variability?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements strengthen scaffold-specific curve learning and weaken universal loading explanations. m128 moved from 39.47/54.40 mL at 10/1 to 33.49/73.97 mL at 20/1, showing that onset need not continue monotonically while completion increases. The m95 series supports endpoint separation: onset changed moderately while completion rose strongly toward 76.31 mL. The m72 DCM/PE comparison showed a noticeable onset difference but similar completion, whereas the matched m173 loading-solvent-volume extension was nearly unchanged, so protocol effects remain conditional. The m73 repeat measured 4.73/9.74 mL after an earlier invalid or reversed record, and m194 again showed a much shorter completion at low loading; these outcomes argue against fitting isolated long-completion branches as universal loading rules. I therefore prioritize new local curves for high-error heteroaromatic, donor-containing, and multifunctional families, with matched endpoint and loading contrasts where they can discriminate transfer hypotheses.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates on transferable failure repair while retaining chemically meaningful local curves. Three matched or near-matched groups address isomer and connectivity transfer: m160/m161, m211, and m146. Additional paired curves target measured high-retention failures in m199, m37, m90, m118, m114, and m216. The alcohol, phenol, amino-ester, and aldehyde choices cover donor-rich silica interactions represented by the large errors in m206, m207, m209, m87, m88, m89, m197, and related polar families. m45 and m11 add local acid and strongly polar nitrogen response points, and m72 provides a loading-protocol contrast after the previous mixed protocol feedback. The selected rows span weak through strong PE/EA ratios, several loading amounts, and both loading solvents, but the contrasts are tied to specific structures rather than used as an assumed universal loading law. This should improve the learned structure-condition-retention mapping and separate onset from completion across high-width regions that recur throughout the Row-distribution.
